<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via system_permissions (symbol, a field of interface PermissionSetRowForDefinition), tab_permissions (symbol, a field of interface PermissionSetRowForDefinition))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via system_permissions (symbol, a field of interface PermissionSetRowForDefinition), tab_permissions (symbol, a field of interface PermissionSetRowForDefinition))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e7057d7a693986a4651a5bd5cbbb5831130a914e` — the merge of head `74b7c06c6b4422f23533aff3a65bf2841a48d13f` into base `6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e7057d7a693986a4651a5bd5cbbb5831130a914e && git checkout e7057d7a693986a4651a5bd5cbbb5831130a914e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672 74b7c06c6b4422f23533aff3a65bf2841a48d13f && git checkout -B drift-repro 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672 && git merge --no-ff 74b7c06c6b4422f23533aff3a65bf2841a48d13f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

CI red, not this PR's · `domain:engine` seat 2 (#20966) · `os-steve` · `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX` · 2026-10-12T05:53Z.

- **What failed:** `Test Core (6/6)` → "Check this shard's timing drift" on head `e975c410bc` (run `38207957661`): `2954.1s measured vs 1818.0s predicted across 11 package(s) = 1.62x`. Every other step of the shard is green, and all its declared tests are accounted for.
- **Why it is not this PR's:** the overshoot sits in packages this diff does not touch: `runtime` 1.73x, `service-analytics` 2.39x, `rest` 1.41x and `client` 2.12x. Two other PRs that change packages low in the graph went red on the same step at the same ratio within 25 minutes (PR #22953 at 1.60x, PR #22954 at 1.61x), while `main`'s runs since the 2026-10-12 dataset refresh are green. Filed fresh as #22966, as #22917's landing record asks.
- **Fix:** none exists yet. The step forbids hand-editing the dataset or raising its 1.5x bound, so the remedy is #22966's to route.
- **Re-run:** this seat has no means to re-run a job. The relay carries no re-run op. The patch round already in progress on this PR (changeset wording, from the contract record) will push a new head, which runs CI afresh. If that head goes red on this step alone, the PR waits on #22966 and is not armed red.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e975c410bc26a1eae2f3f322cbc50e5b6c913ae6`
Local-runs: none

PR #22959 (card #22937, PR 1 of 2) at the head above, read against `origin/main` `51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501`, which is also the merge base: six files, +483/−0, additions only. Inputs: the card body and both of its comments (claim 6117549106, os-dev-report 6118339780); #15211's body with the seat answer 6110777865 (E5 → A) and its note 6110790598; the PR body, its one comment, its file list and the three-dot diff; the check-runs on the head; and, on `origin/main`, the plugin-security originals, core's `security/index.ts` and `position-binding-conversion.ts`, `PermissionSetSchema`, `PositionSchema`, and the two `export *` sites.

### ① Derived judgments

**Surface added — right.** `security/index.ts` gains two export blocks directly after the `convertPositionBindingRows` block: `permissionSetDefinitionFromRow` with `type PermissionSetRowForDefinition`, and `positionDefinitionFromRow` with `type PositionRowForDefinition`. Core's root `src/index.ts` runs `export * from './security/index.js'`, so all four land on `@objectstack/core`'s published `.` entry; `./logger` is untouched. `@objectstack/runtime` (`src/index.ts`) and `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` (`src/adapter.ts`) each run `export * from '@objectstack/core'` and so re-export the two functions and two types. Collision: none — `git grep` of the four names on `origin/main` returns nothing, on the head they occur only under `packages/core/src/security/` and in the changeset, and neither re-exporting package declares a local of those names, so the star re-export is unambiguous.

**Equivalence with the originals — right, judged by reading the pairs side by side.**
- `permissionSetDefinitionFromRow` against `permissionSetBodyFromRow` (`permission-set-projection.ts`). The candidate object is the same literal in the same order: `name`; `label: row?.label ?? row?.name`; a conditional `description` spread on `row?.description != null` (an empty string travels, `null` and absent do not); `objects`, `fields`, `systemPermissions`, `rowLevelSecurity`, `tabPermissions` through `parseMaybeJson` with the same defaults (`{}`, `{}`, `[]`, `[]`, `{}`); then a conditional `adminScope` spread. `adminScope` is computed first in both and travels only when the column is truthy AND parses to a truthy value, so `''`, `'null'`, `'false'`, `'0'`, unparseable text and `null` all leave it absent. `parseMaybeJson` is copied verbatim: a non-string answers itself, or the fallback when nullish; `''` is parsed as JSON `null`; a parsed `null` and a throw both answer the fallback; the default is a fresh object per call. The spec-key filter is the plugin's `permissionSpecBodyKeys` plus `pickSpecDeclaredKeys` folded into the function: the same `Object.keys(PermissionSetSchema.shape ?? {})`, memoised on first call rather than at import (the schema is a `lazySchema` proxy, the plugin's own reason), and the same `Object.entries` loop, so key order is insertion order. `strictObject` returns a `closedObject` built from the `z.object(...).strict()` def, so `.shape` is present, and the plugin's production code already depends on that read. The nine emitted keys (`name`, `label`, `description`, `objects`, `fields`, `systemPermissions`, `rowLevelSecurity`, `tabPermissions`, `adminScope`) are all declared on `PermissionSetSchema`, so the filter removes nothing today and the pin reddens on a rename. A `null` or `undefined` row answers `{ name: undefined, label: undefined, objects: {}, fields: {}, systemPermissions: [], rowLevelSecurity: [], tabPermissions: {} }` in both. The differences are type-level only: the original takes and returns `any`; the copy takes `PermissionSetRowForDefinition | null | undefined` (the named optional columns plus a string index signature, all `unknown`) and returns a string-keyed record of `unknown` values. The PR body's "the type the plugin's copies return" is exact for `positionBodyFromRow` and loose for `permissionSetBodyFromRow`, which returns `any`; no caller-visible consequence for the 7a switch-over.
- `positionDefinitionFromRow` against `positionBodyFromRow` (`position-write-through.ts`, which `position-environment-backfill.ts` imports and applies — the dev located the mapping correctly where the card's pointer named the backfill file). Identical statement for statement: `name` as stored; `label` when a non-empty string, else the name; `description` only when a non-empty string (so `null`, `''`, absent and a non-string are all absent); `delegatable` always present and `true` for exactly `true`, `1`, `'1'`, `'true'`. Key order `name`, `label`, `description`, `delegatable`. Both dereference `row.name` directly, so a `null` or `undefined` row throws in both; the copy's parameter type refuses `null` at compile time, which is honest about that. The asymmetry with the permission-set function, which tolerates a null row, is inherited from the originals, not introduced.

**Purity and no behaviour change — right.** Neither function performs I/O, touches an engine, or mutates its input (the pins freeze the row); the only module state is the memoised key set, a constant. Nothing calls either function: the four names occur nowhere outside the two new modules, their tests, the barrel and the changeset. Neither runs at boot. No existing export changes shape.

**No validation, no name judgement — right, as the docblocks say.** Neither function calls `safeParse`, tests `METADATA_ITEM_NAME_PATTERN`, or reads `PositionSchema.shape.name`; `metadataDoorAcceptsPositionName` stays in plugin-security. The position pin asserts a capitalised name still answers a body; the permission-set pins assert an off-contract facet still answers a body and a well-formed row's body passes `PermissionSetSchema.safeParse`.

**No dependency added; lean closure held — right.** `packages/core/package.json` is not in the diff. The only new runtime import is `PermissionSetSchema` from `@objectstack/spec/security`, a module core already loads values from (`api-key.ts`, `effective-object-permissions.ts`, `resolve-authz-context.ts`, `deployment-org-scoping-entitlement.ts`); the proxy is not materialised until the first call, so core's load does not grow. `position-row-definition.ts` imports nothing. The position test imports `PositionSchema` from `@objectstack/spec/identity` — core's first import of that subpath, test-only, inside the already-declared workspace package. `check:lean-entry-closure` asserts a package SET, and no package enters it.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-security/**` untouched — right.** The file list is `.changeset/22937-core-row-definition-mappers.md`, `packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, the two new modules and their two tests. Nothing under `content/docs/permissions/`, `content/docs/releases/` or any `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Changeset, sentence by sentence against the code.** Frontmatter `"@objectstack/core": minor` — right (②). Title — right. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — right (②).
- "What is new … the upgrade ceremony (`os migrate`) applies them to save Setup-authored rows through the metadata door. ⛔ Neither runs at boot." The exports, the home beside `convertPositionBindingRows` and "never at boot" are right. "applies them" is present tense while PR 2 is unbuilt; the final bullet, "nothing calls them yet", corrects it inside the same text, and `origin/main` already describes `convertPositionBindingRows` the same way in a published migration entry (`18.position-permission-sets-declared.ts`) with no caller either. Follows house precedent; "is to apply" would be tighter.
- "The permission-set mapping … `admin_scope` → `adminScope` when set." The five facet renames are right; "when set" compresses "a truthy column that parses to a truthy value", which the docblock spells out. "`label` falls back to the name." Right for `null` and absent; the condition is unstated here while the position sentence states its own, and the two mappings differ on `''` (kept for a permission set, replaced by the name for a position). "A facet that is absent, empty or unparseable answers its default." Right, with `null` and JSON `null` unlisted; the docblock lists them (commit `dd1e7d44424c` added them there and not here). "The body keeps only the keys `PermissionSetSchema` declares, so `active`, `managed_by`, `customized` and the timestamps never travel." The first clause is right; the "so" is not the mechanism — those columns never enter the candidate, and the filter removes nothing today. The stated outcome is true.
- "The position mapping … a `null` or blank `description` is absent". **"Blank" does not describe the rule the code applies.** The test is `typeof row.description === 'string' && row.description !== ''`: only the empty string is dropped, a whitespace-only description travels, and a non-string one is dropped. The word is copied from the plugin original's own docblock, where it carries the same imprecision; in a CHANGELOG line "empty" is the accurate word. The `label` and `delegatable` clauses and "`active` and `is_default` are row state and never travel" are right.
- "No behaviour changes … the same output as … `permissionSetBodyFromRow` and `positionBodyFromRow`, and nothing calls them yet. Neither validates …" Right, by the side-by-side read above.

Net: no sentence misstates the exported surface or its semver; four sentences are looser than the code, and one of them ("blank") is strictly false for a whitespace-only description. These are wording corrections to one file; the seat may ask for them before arming, and a new head then needs a fresh record on it.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/core` `minor` — right. Two value exports and two type exports are added to a published entry and nothing is removed or narrowed: a purely additive widening, which the ruling `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` mechanises prices at least `minor`, on the one package whose `src/**` moved. `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` widen transitively through `export *`; their `src/**` did not move, so the gate asks nothing of them, and their bump arrives through changesets' internal-dependency propagation at version time. `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head.

`Clause-②` — one value, written three ways: PR body line 2 `yes`, changeset `yes (widening)`, claim `yes`. The arm is optional (`clause2-line.mjs`: an absent arm is "the overwhelming live shape"), carries no breaking signal, and `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` pins both spellings as a non-breaking widening in its own self-tests. The dev's deviation note ("not a conflict") is right. The value is true: the published surface widens.

ADR-0087 marker — none owed. The gate judges only a changeset that declares a breaking change; a `minor` carrying `Clause-②: yes` or `yes (widening)` is, by the gate's own rule, not breaking; no spec key moves; no registry entry exists to cite. The dev's run of the gate exited 0; CI's copy rides in `Lint & Repo Gates`, pending at the final read.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **No closing keyword.** Right for PR 1 of 2: `Part of #22937` and `Part of #15211`; PR 2 completes the card. `Part-of PR must not also close its card` and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` both concluded `success`; the newest `Claim:` on the card names this branch and this session.
- **Backfill decisions left in plugin-security** (`metadataDoorAcceptsPositionName`; the rows-of-one-name-must-agree check). Inside the card's scope: E5 → A moves "the row-to-definition mapping", and the card forbids plugin-security edits. Both decisions decide what to WRITE, which is PR 2's per-name call; the door's own refusal covers the grammar meanwhile. The core mapping's key order is pinned (the serialisation-equality test), so an agreement check over its output stays meaningful. Carrier as the dev names it: PR 2 and 7b. Answered; no escalation.
- **S8 overlap in `security/index.ts`.** On `origin/main` the `isRowActive` export is line 245; this PR inserts after line 280, the close of the `position-binding-conversion.js` block, with 35 untouched lines between — distinct hunks, so a text merge applies cleanly in either landing order, and neither new file imports `row-active.ts`. Answered.
- **Uncommitted equivalence harness.** Acceptable: core cannot import plugin-security without inverting the dependency, plugin-security is closed to this card, and the measurement is evidence to weigh, not to repeat. Equivalence stands here on the side-by-side read in ①; the permanent proof is 7a/7b deleting the plugin copies. The committed pins assert the documented outputs and carry the one spec-rename tripwire that matters.
- **Commit trailers and footer.** The two authored commits end with the model-free pair AGENTS.md prescribes; the PR body ends with the session-URL footer under a rule line, the body form. The harness reminder's model-named trailer yields to AGENTS.md by its own precedence sentence; right. The merge commit, which is the head, carries git's default message and no trailer pair — a squash landing replaces it, and the pre-push hook refuses a model identifier, not an absence. Noted; no action.
- **First gate derivation in the shared checkout.** A read-only `dispatch-gates.mjs` derivation that wrote nothing (exit 2), then re-derived from the worktree; Prime Directive 11 governs edits, and none occurred. Reported as a deviation, which is the right handling; not verifiable from the inputs beyond the report, and harmless by construction. Answered.
- **Other `deviations` and the report's lists.** Battery 1's timeouts and dist-less gates are superseded by the final 63/63 union at this head — accepted on the dev's own reconciliation; CI's required contexts are the verdicts here. One merge of `origin/main` before opening (docs and workflows only); the merge base equals `origin/main`'s tip, so the three-dot diff is a clean delta. `open_questions`: empty. `out_of_scope_findings`: the three answered above, each noted rather than filed — right under Prime Directive 10, since none is a defect, a contract violation or an authoring trap.
- **Docs drift advisory** (PR comment 6118319857). `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx` is listed through a column-name coincidence (`system_permissions` and `tab_permissions` as fields of the new interface). No behaviour changes; no page owes an edit.
- **Check-runs on the head, at the final read.** Completed, every one `success` or `skipped`: `Build Core`; `Dogfood Regression Gate` and its three shards; `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`; `Governed Surface Queue Guard`; `TypeScript Type Check` and its four sub-jobs; `Check Changeset`; `Check PR Size`; `Dogfood Verify CLI`; the two claim checks and the Part-of check; `Flag docs affected by code changes`. **Still in progress: `Lint & Repo Gates`, and `Test Core (1/6)` through `Test Core (6/6)`** — both required contexts. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record does not vouch for them, and the seat arms only once each reads `success`.
- The PR is a draft, as the card asked; flipping it is the seat's act, after the two pending contexts conclude.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-22937-core-row-definition-mappers`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX`

**VERDICT: PASS**


Adopted by `domain:engine#2` (`session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX`) at 2026-10-12T05:55Z. The record came from an isolated at-tier reviewer. Its transcript shows read-only tool use: REST reads, a fetch into a review ref and `git show` reads, and its only write was its own scratch record. Following the record's finding, the seat asked for the changeset corrections before arming: the false "blank" sentence and the four loose ones. The dev made them, with no code change, in commit `d477e5fbef` (patch round 1, report 6118594623). The seat corrected the matching PR-body line. This PASS covers `e975c410bc`. A delta record on `d477e5fbef` follows before the PR is armed. The `Test Core (6/6)` red on `e975c410bc` is the timing-drift step alone, filed as #22966.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d477e5fbef0f89677a44b55eb93ec1e170497987`
Local-runs: none

Delta record for PR #22959 (card #22937, PR 1 of 2). The branch gained exactly one commit since the PASS record on `e975c410bc26a1eae2f3f322cbc50e5b6c913ae6`: `d477e5fbef`, parent `e975c410bc`, no merge of `main`. Inputs: the PR body (the seat's edited `permissionSetDefinitionFromRow` bullet included), its three comments (the prior record with the seat's adoption note, the seat's CI comment naming #22966, the docs-drift advisory), its file list; the card's three comments, patch-round report 6118594623 among them; the delta `git diff e975c410bc refs/review/pr-22959` and the three-dot diff against `origin/main` (merge base `51b43a8dc`, unchanged; six files, +483/−0); the check-runs on the head; on the head, `permission-set-row-definition.ts` and `position-row-definition.ts`; on `origin/main`, `permissionSetBodyFromRow` and `parseMaybeJson` in `permission-set-projection.ts` and `positionBodyFromRow` in `position-write-through.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

**The delta changes no code — right.** Three files, +5/−5. `.changeset/22937-core-row-definition-mappers.md`: three bullets rewritten. `position-row-definition.ts`: one line inside the module docblock (the block opens at line 3 and closes at line 42; the edit is line 26). `position-row-definition.test.ts`: one line comment at line 88. Blob identity across the two heads: `permission-set-row-definition.ts` `987eabe8d0` on both, `security/index.ts` `397a792ba1` on both; `position-row-definition.ts` moves from `e768032fef` to `2f23f68e0a` by that one docblock line. No statement, type, export or test assertion moves. The two functions, the two row types, the barrel's two export blocks and the 21 pins are byte-for-byte what the prior record judged, so no accept set and no public surface it judged has changed; its equivalence, purity, no-dependency and no-collision findings carry over unaltered.

**Each rewritten sentence, read against the code on the head and against the plugin originals on `origin/main`.**

- Changeset, "What is new": "The upgrade ceremony (`os migrate`) is to apply them, to save Setup-authored rows through the metadata door." Right. Nothing calls either function (the four names occur only in the two modules, their tests, the barrel and the changeset); PR 2 carries the `--apply`. This is the wording the prior record called tighter. The two module docblocks and the barrel comment keep their present tense ("converts it: it reads the row, calls this function"; "applied by the ceremony"); they were not rewritten, the prior record read them without objection, and `origin/main` describes `convertPositionBindingRows` the same way. Not owed.
- Changeset, "The permission-set mapping", `adminScope`: "only when the column is truthy and reads to a truthy value." Right. `const adminScope = row?.admin_scope ? parseMaybeJson(row.admin_scope, undefined) : undefined` then `...(adminScope ? { adminScope } : {})`: a falsy column (`null`, `''`, absent) and a truthy column whose parse is falsy (`'0'`, `'false'`, `'null'`, `'""'`, unparseable text) both leave the key absent; an already-parsed object is truthy and travels. Identical in `permissionSetBodyFromRow`.
- Same bullet, `label`: "falls back to the name only when the column is `null` or absent; an empty-string label is kept (unlike the position rule below)." Right. `label: row?.label ?? row?.name` is nullish coalescing: `''` is kept; the position rule replaces `''` with the name. Identical in the original.
- Same bullet, facet defaults: "A facet column that is `null`, absent, an empty string, JSON `null` or unparseable text answers its default; a facet a driver already parsed is kept as it is." Right, clause by clause against `parseMaybeJson`: a non-string answers itself or, when nullish, the fallback (so `null` and absent answer the default and a parsed object is kept); `''` is parsed as the text `null`; a parsed `null` and a thrown parse both answer the fallback. The copy is verbatim from the original.
- Same bullet, read-then-filter: "Only the definition columns are read, so `active`, `managed_by`, `customized` and the timestamps never enter the body. The body is then filtered to the keys `PermissionSetSchema` declares." Right, and the mechanism the prior record said the old "so" misstated is now the one the code applies: the candidate literal reads exactly `name`, `label`, `description`, `object_permissions`, `field_permissions`, `system_permissions`, `row_level_security`, `tab_permissions` and `admin_scope`; the `Object.entries` loop then keeps the keys in `permissionSpecBodyKeys()`, read from `PermissionSetSchema.shape`.
- Changeset, "The position mapping", `label`: "falls back to the name unless it is a non-empty string (so `''` is replaced by the name)." Right: `typeof row.label === 'string' && row.label !== '' ? row.label : row.name`.
- Same bullet, `description`: "travels only when it is a non-empty string: `null`, `''`, an absent column and a non-string are absent, and a whitespace-only string travels as stored." Right: `if (typeof row.description === 'string' && row.description !== '') body.description = row.description`.
